## Goal

De-risk the arena's campaign integration (AH-0MV8QT7CB0060A7A) before any build work: prove the shared campaign and upgrade-choice systems can run headless under Node/vitest with the same seed derivation the game uses, and identify every impure dependency so the design uses the shared core directly or a named thin adapter — never a divergent copy.

## Headline

A short spike that instantiates/runs the modules the arena will consume — `buildSequencedLevels` (src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts, all fixed/curve/dynamic modes), `sequencer`/`defaultCandidatePool` (src/core/difficultySequencer.ts), `WaveManager` (src/waves/WaveManager.ts), `chooseOptions`/`buildChoiceCandidates` (src/powerups/choice.ts), `MineralHold` (src/core/GameState.ts hold), and the hold-full reward application path (`applyMineralChoiceReward`, src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts) — and records exactly which are headless-pure and which need an adapter (e.g. the `EffectsRegistry` the reward applyer requires).

## Context

- The eval layer (src/ai/eval/) must stay pure: no wall clock, no I/O, no Phaser import.
- Gym↔game parity (AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1): an enabled behaviour runs the same code in gym/game and in the eval arena.
- Effort-and-risk unknowns recorded on the parent: can `sequencedLevels.ts` run headless without Phaser imports? Can the reward-application path be exercised without a Phaser `EffectsRegistry`?

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1:** A vitest smoke test imports and exercises each target module without importing Phaser or a wall-clock/IO module in the eval entry path; the smoke test lives under src/ai/eval/ (e.g. a `campaignHeadless.test.ts` spike scaffold).
- **AC2:** Every impure dependency found is listed with a concrete adapter plan (thin, named, headless) or a recommendation to not model that behaviour in this item — recorded in a comment on this work item.
- **AC3:** The spike records the design decision the arena build follows: consume each shared entry point directly vs via the named adapter, with the seed derivation (createSeededRng + buildSequencedLevels {seed}) confirmed to be deterministic.
- **AC4:** The spike makes no production code changes outside src/ai/eval/ evaluation-only scaffolding; the finding is reproducible by a maintainer (commands recorded).

## Key Files

**Key Files:**
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` — campaign builder (fixed/curve/dynamic modes) to prove headless-safe
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts` — sequencer + candidate pool to prove headless-safe
- `src/waves/WaveManager.ts` — wave/level state machine to prove headless-safe
- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — shared upgrade-choice flow to prove headless-safe
- `src/core/GameState.ts` — MineralHold (capacity/growth/overflow)
- `src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts` — applyMineralChoiceReward (EffectsRegistry dependency to assess)
- `src/ai/eval/campaignHeadless.test.ts` (new vitest spike scaffold) — headless-import smoke coverage
data.title: Spike: prove the shared campaign core runs headless (wave sequencer + upgrade choices)

# Not all power-ups are appearing in the hull-full (hold-full) screen

> **Headline:** Restore full catalogue coverage in the hold-full choice overlay — every power-up and weapon drop (except the `reset` utility) must have a chance of appearing.

## Problem statement

The hold-full choice overlay (`MineralChoiceScene`) draws its options from the static
`CHOICE_POOL` list in `src/powerups/choice.ts`, which has not kept pace with the
catalogue. Ten shipped drops never appear: the five net-new power-ups (`frenzy`,
`chrono`, `thorns`, `salvage`, `strike`) and the five net-new weapons (`rear_guard`,
`broadside`, `railgun`, `shard_swarm`, `heavy_slug`). An exhaustive test pins the
stale 21-entry list, so the gap is invisible to the suite. All ten should have a
chance of appearing when the hold fills.

## Users

- **Player** — fills the mineral hold, opens the hold-full choice, and expects any
  power-up/weapon he has ever seen in the field (or the catalogue) to be a candidate.
  - *As a player, I want Frenzy, Chrono Field, Thorn Field, Salvage and Orbital
    Strike to be offered when my hold fills, so I can build toward the power-up
    I am collecting, rather than only ever being able to earn them as field drops.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Pool covers the full catalogue, with no gating.** `CHOICE_POOL` contains every
  power-up id (`frenzy`, `chrono`, `thorns`, `salvage`, `strike` added) and every weapon id
  (`rear_guard`, `broadside`, `railgun`, `shard_swarm`, `heavy_slug` added), minus `reset`
  only, with no unlock-state filter and no per-scene copies. A regression test asserts the
  pool equals the full catalogue minus `reset`, replacing the stale exhaustive assertion in
  `src/powerups/__tests__/choice.test.ts`.
- **AC2 — New options are fully functional when picked.** Each of the ten added ids,
  selected as a base grant in the hold-full choice, applies through the existing shared
  reward path (`applyMineralChoiceReward` + `effectsRegistry.applyCollect`), renders a
  name/description from the shared catalogues (`getHelpDescription`/`WEAPON_NAMES`/
  `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE`), carries the ★ New badge when unowned, and behaves identically
  whether granted in the game (`PlayScene`) or a gym (`GymFormationScene`,
  `GymWeaponLeveling`).
- **AC3 — Ownership/level-up offers continue to work for the new ids.** `buildChoiceCandidates`
  suppresses the base entry for an owned new item and emits its `weapon-level`/`power-up-level`
  offer with a correct `changeSummary`, for each of the ten new ids (the five weapons are
  already in `LEVELABLE_WEAPON_IDS`; the five power-ups already have level curves).
- **AC4 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes,** including code
  comments (`src/powerups/choice.ts` module prose), the GDD §4.5 pool description
  ("all power-ups plus Spread/Dual/Rapid/Nova/Mortar/Arc") and any affected test docs.
- **AC5 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.** The Power Pellet
  removal guard (`powerPelletRemoval.test.ts`) and the choice-strategy suite remain green,
  with the "does not over-remove" guard extended to all sixteen power-ups.

## Constraints

- **Keep the pool single-source.** The game and every gym must consume the same
  `CHOICE_POOL`/`randomChoiceStrategy`; no divergent per-scene copies (gym↔game parity,
  AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1).
- **No weighting change.** Base-entry weights stay uniform at 1.0× with the existing
  1.35× owned-upgrade bonus (Q3-A); this item fixes eligibility only. Field-drop rarity
  tuning is out of scope.
- **No unlock-state gating** (Q2-N/A): the mini-boss locked pool is being retired.
- **`reset` stays excluded** — it removes weapons rather than granting one (documented).
- **Do not touch the `unlocks.ts` machinery**; removal of the locked pool is owned by
  AH-0MVLISU03006WDOD. This item only widens the choice pool.

## Existing state

- `CHOICE_POOL` (`src/powerups/choice.ts`) — 21 entries: 11 power-ups + 10 weapons.
- Stale exhaustive assertion in `src/powerups/__tests__/choice.test.ts` pins exactly
  those 21 ids.
- The ten missing ids already exist everywhere else: `types.ts` catalogue, `rules.ts`
  weight tables (`POWER_UP_WEIGHT_IDS`/`WEAPON_WEIGHT_IDS`, `defaultPowerUpWeights`/
  `defaultWeaponWeights`), `effects.ts` registry, `powerUpLevels.ts` curves, `icons.ts`,
  HUD, gym help — only the hold-full pool omits them.
- `LEVELABLE_WEAPON_IDS` already includes the five new weapons; `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE`
  already includes the five new power-ups — so level-up/ownership paths need no new code.

## Desired change

Add the ten missing ids to `CHOICE_POOL`; the pool becomes every power-up and weapon
drop id except `reset` (16 + 15 = 31 entries). Update/extend the regression tests so the
pool can never silently drift from the catalogue again, and refresh the stale docs
(choice module prose + GDD §4.5). No change to the selection strategy, weighting,
reward application, or unlock machinery.

## Key Files

- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — add the ten ids to `CHOICE_POOL`; refresh module doc:
  "the base drop pool (Shield–Mineral Scoop plus the collectable weapon drops …)".
- `src/powerups/__tests__/choice.test.ts` — replace the exhaustive 21-entry assertion
  with a catalogue-derived invariant (pool ⊇ all power-up ids ∪ all weapon ids minus `reset`).
- `src/powerups/powerPelletRemoval.test.ts` — extend `REMAINING_POWER_UP_IDS` to the full
  sixteen so the "does not over-remove" guard covers the net-new power-ups.
- `src/powerups/unlocks.ts` / `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — **no change** (locked-pool
  removal is a separate item); verify only.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §4.5 hold-full pool wording ("all power-ups plus
  Spread/Dual/Rapid/Nova/Mortar/Arc" → full catalogue minus `reset`).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` —
  consume the widened default pool automatically; verify gym tests that assert offered sets.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** "hull-full screen" == the hold-full choice overlay
  (`MineralChoiceScene`), opened when the mineral hold fills (GDD §4.5); "hull" is a
  mistyping of "hold". Confirmed by the operator's answers referencing hold-full behaviour.
- **Assumption (AC1):** the locked-pool retirement (AH-0MVLISU03006WDOD) will land;
  until it does, a hold-full grant of a formerly-locked weapon is acceptable (they already
  drop in the field via the weight tables).
- **Risk — widening dilutes the pool:** holding the option count at 3 while the pool grows
  from 21 → 31 makes each specific pick slightly rarer. Accepted by Q3-A (uniform
  weighting kept); rebalance is a candidate follow-up item if playtests complain.
- **Risk — gym test drift:** gym launchers inherit the widened pool automatically; tests
  asserting exact option sets may need updates — accounted for in AC2.
- **Scope creep guard:** rarity tuning for field weights, the mini-boss reward UI
  (AH-0MVLISU03006WDOD) and `unlocks.ts` changes are *not* part of this item.

## Related work

- AH-0MVI4KTD8000FBJ7 — this work item.
- AH-0MVLISU03006WDOD — "Mini-Boss rewards become valuable": removes the locked-pool
  reward system; makes this item's no-gating decision stable (`related-to`).
- AH-0MVCRBNO6003E1CH — "Mini-boss reward: upgrade-or-unlock + locked pool": origin of
  the locked weapons now entering the pool.
- AH-0MVCRC1Q0007JAV1 / AH-0MVCC8XSS007P01Z — epic introducing the five net-new power-ups
  (frenzy/chrono/thorns/salvage/strike).
- AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1 — gym↔game parity (single shared implementation).
- AH-0MUY47W62005FF74 / AH-0MVCFB00Y004AQ2Z — owned-upgrade 1.35× weighting (unchanged).
- AH-0MV5CB6KO0079N08 — Power Pellet removal guard (must stay green).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Which missing drops should enter the hold-full pool — (A) only the 5 net-new
  power-ups, or (B) the power-ups **and** the 5 mini-boss-locked weapons?"
  — Answer (operator): **B** — both categories; pool = every drop id except `reset`.
  Source: interactive reply in intake session.
  Research: `CHOICE_POOL` holds 21 ids vs 16 + 16 in the catalogue; the only missing
  weapons are the five locked ones (`reset` is a documented exclusion).
- Q2: "Should the five mini-boss-locked weapons respect the mini-boss unlock state in the
  hold-full pool?"
  — Answer (operator): **N/A** — "We are changing the mini-boss rewards system in another
  work item, there will no longer be mini-boss locked items, all powerups will be offered
  as normal powerups." Source: interactive reply. Evidence: AH-0MVLISU03006WDOD
  ("Mini-Boss rewards become valuable", open, stage `idea`) describes a wheel-based
  reward replacing the locked-pool choice; no unlock gating required here.
- Q3: "Weighting within the hold-full pool — (A) keep uniform base-entry weight, or
  (B) mirror field-drop rarity?"
  — Answer (operator): **A** — keep uniform; fix eligibility only. Source: interactive
  reply. Rationale: report is about absence, not rarity.

## How to verify

```bash
# Changed-scope gate (unit + smoke) via the project test skill:
/skill:test

# Targeted inspection while implementing:
rg -n "CHOICE_POOL" src/powerups/choice.ts
```

## Validation notes

- The ten missing ids were computed directly from the source (`types.ts` type unions vs
  `CHOICE_POOL`) — see the intake session's scripted diff (16 power-ups, 16 weapons,
  pool 21, missing `frenzy, chrono, thorns, salvage, strike` and
  `rear_guard, broadside, railgun, shard_swarm, heavy_slug`).
- Duplicate check performed: `wl search` for power-up/hold-full/keywords found no
  overlapping open item addressing pool eligibility (`discovered-from` AH-0MVLISU03006WDOD
  is a different mechanism change).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUQOVYZU0073OUV** – Feature: Permanent mineral-choice weapon leveling (completed)
- **AH-0MUVRACE9001WVT2** – Level-up offers duplicate weapon (basic + upgraded version of same weapon) (completed)
- **AH-0MUTPEIZ5002FIJP** – P10 power-up identity — catalogue, spawn pool, choice pool and icon (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0muy47w62005ff74, 0mv5cb6ko0079n08, 0mvcc8xss007p01z, 0mvcfb00y004aq2z, 0mvcrbno6003e1ch (+329 more)
- `README.md` — matched: 0muy47w62005ff74, 0mvcc8xss007p01z, 0mvcfb00y004aq2z, able, ac1 (+321 more)

# Salvage has no visible effect (AH-0MVJ72I8O0009T09)

## Problem statement

While the **Salvage** bounty window is active, each destroyed non-hazard enemy
drops the level-resolved bonus minerals at the wreck, but those minerals render
as exactly the same gold dots as every ordinary mineral. The bounty therefore
has no *visible* effect: the player cannot tell whether the extra minerals came
from Salvage, and the pickup feels inert even though the mechanic is wired.

## Users and user stories

- **Player (bounty chooser):** *As a player who collected or chose Salvage, when
  I destroy an enemy I want the bonus minerals to look different from ordinary
  minerals, so I can see the bounty paying out and judge whether it was worth
  the pickup.*
- **Player (economy reading):** *As a player reading the mineral field, I want
  ordinary mineral drops to stay gold, so the baseline economy stays readable
  and the orange dots uniquely mean "Salvage bonus".*

## Current behaviour (verified in the repo)

- `EffectsRegistry.salvageBonusMinerals()` (`src/powerups/effects.ts`) returns
  `0` unless the timed window is active, otherwise the level-resolved
  `salvageMinerals` (curve base **1** → cap **4**, k=0.35).
- The shared kill seam adds exactly that many extra minerals at the wreck
  through `scatterMineralDrops(...)`:
  - `PlayScene` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, in the kill handler, just after
    `resolveMineralKillDrops`);
  - `GymFormationScene._dropMineralsForKill`
    (`src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`).
  Both guard with `isNonBlockingHazard(...)` / the `getSizeTier` test, so
  **asteroids and lane hazards are excluded** — Salvage pays out for destroyed
  **ships** only, even though the original report assumed "ships and/or
  asteroids".
- The HUD already lists a Salvage row while the window is active
  (`src/ui/HUD.ts`, `case 'salvage'` → `reg.isActive(id)`), so a countdown
  readout exists. The visibility gap is purely the **drop rendering**.
- `Mineral` hard-codes `MINERAL_COLOR` (`0xffdd44`, gold) in `_drawBody()`
  (`src/entities/Mineral.ts`), and `scatterMineralDrops` accepts no colour, so
  every mineral in the game and in every gym is visually identical.

## Desired change

Give **Salvage bonus minerals their own colour — orange** — while every other
mineral stays gold, in the game and in every gym, through one shared code path.
The change is cosmetic: an orange salvage mineral is still worth exactly one
mineral.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Orange salvage drops.** While the Salvage window is active, the bonus
   minerals spawned at a destroyed enemy's wreck render **orange**, and every
   other mineral (asteroid drop, enemy re-drop, seeded gym field, drone spill)
   continues to render **gold**. Covered by unit tests in the game
   (`PlayScene`) and in the formation gym (`GymFormationScene`).
2. **Single source of colour.** The orange is defined once as a named constant
   (`MINERAL_SALVAGE_COLOR`) beside `MINERAL_COLOR` in `src/core/constants.ts`;
   `Mineral` accepts an optional colour (default `MINERAL_COLOR`), so all
   existing callers keep the gold default unchanged.
3. **One shared seam (gym↔game parity).** Game and gyms spawn salvage drops
   through **one** shared helper (e.g. `scatterSalvageMineralDrops` next to
   `scatterMineralDrops`), and the repo-wide defined-once guard in
   `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` covers it, so the colour
   and scatter maths cannot drift between `PlayScene` and the gyms.
4. **No behaviour, economy or RNG change.** Each salvage mineral is still worth
   one mineral, the bonus count still comes from
   `salvageBonusMinerals()`, asteroids remain excluded, and the scatter helper
   consumes the same two RNG draws per drop in the same order (existing
   determinism/draw-order tests stay green).
5. **Visible in a real run.** With Salvage active, an enemy kill leaves orange
   dots on the field next to any gold drops, so the effect is legible to the
   player without reading the HUD.
6. **Documentation updated.** The GDD (§4.4 Salvage entry / §4.4.1 minerals
   "Dropping" bullet), `README.md`'s mineral section and the relevant code
   comments all describe the orange salvage drop.
7. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including
   code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
8. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Cosmetic only: no new drop type, no value change, no magnet/scoop behaviour
  change, no HUD redesign.
- Keep the existing `scatterMineralDrops` signature backwards compatible
  (optional colour parameter or an additive helper), so the many current
  callers (asteroid drops, enemy re-drops, collector-drone spill, gym seeding)
  are untouched.
- The orange must be clearly distinct from gold and from existing gameplay
  colours (enemy fire reds/pinks, power-up bubble colours); confirm the chosen
  value against the bullet/pickup palettes before picking it.
- No new procedural timers or per-frame work — this is a fill colour at spawn.

## Existing state

- Salvage is already fully wired (`AH-0MVH80ZJ7009W18Z`): bonus minerals spawn
  through the shared kill seam in `PlayScene` and `GymFormationScene`, and the
  integration test `AH-0MVH80ZJ7009W18Z — Salvage adds bonus minerals at a
  destroyed enemy` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`) proves the count grows.
- The only missing piece is a distinguishable render colour for those drops.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/constants.ts` — add `MINERAL_SALVAGE_COLOR` (orange) with a doc
  comment next to `MINERAL_COLOR`.
- `src/entities/Mineral.ts` — optional `color` on `MineralConfig`, `_drawBody()`
  uses `config.color ?? MINERAL_COLOR`, plus an optional colour argument (or
  additive helper) on the scatter function.
- `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.ts` — shared re-export / seam for the
  salvage-coloured scatter helper so both scenes import one thing.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — use the shared salvage-drop helper.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — use the same shared salvage-drop
  helper (parity).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — extend the defined-once
  guard to the new helper.
- Tests: `src/entities/__tests__/Mineral.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` (or
  `src/scenes/__tests__/PlayScene.minerals.test.ts`), a
  `GymFormationScene` salvage-colour test, and
  `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.test.ts` if the seam lives there.
- Docs: `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§4.4 Salvage entry and the §4.4.1
  minerals "Dropping" bullet) and `README.md` (minerals section).

## Related work

- **AH-0MVH80ZJ7009W18Z — Some power-ups appear to do nothing (completed):** wired
  `salvageBonusMinerals()` into the shared kill seam (game + gyms). This item is
  the visual follow-up to that wiring.
- **AH-0MVCRC1Q0007JAV1 — 5 net-new power-ups (completed):** introduced the
  Salvage catalogue entry, its level curves (1 → 4 bonus minerals, 10 → 20 s)
  and the HUD readout.
- **AH-0MUBVGI62004ED9Q — Asteroids drop collectable minerals that fill the
  ship's hold (completed):** owns the `Mineral` entity, `MINERAL_COLOR` and the
  shared scatter maths this change extends.
- **AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1 — Document gym-parity principle (completed):** the rule
  that an enabled behaviour runs the same code in the game and every gym; this
  brief therefore demands one shared salvage-drop helper.
- **AH-0MV6M2M9P0078N4S — Asteroids drop more lives (completed):** precedent for
  a kill-drop variant added to the same shared kill seam.
- Repo/docs: `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4 (Salvage) and §4.4.1
  (Minerals, the Ship's Hold & the Power-Up Choice); `README.md` minerals
  section; `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.ts` (shared kill-drop rule).

### Automated find-related report

- **AH-0MTG5MGPZ00986B4** – Power ups need to be larger (completed)
- **AH-0MV6M2M9P0078N4S** – Asteroids drop more lives (completed)
- **AH-0MU8FOQM0007D94Z** – Enemy Config + Factory Wiring + Unit Tests (completed)

Repository file matches: `README.md`, `docs/Game Design Document.md`,
`docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`.

## Out of scope (follow-up candidates, not this item)

- Adding a HUD "Salvage +N" bonus suffix or a pickup flourish. If the colour
  alone proves insufficient, raise a `discovered-from:AH-0MVJ72I8O0009T09`
  item rather than widening this one.
- Making Salvage apply to asteroids/hazards (it deliberately does not).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** a distinct colour is enough to make the bounty legible.
  Justification: the complaint is that the extra drops are indistinguishable;
  the HUD already exposes the active window and its bonus level.
- **Risk (visual collision):** orange may read like enemy fire or a hazard.
  Mitigation: pick a hue/saturation clearly outside the enemy-bullet palette,
  keep the small-dot silhouette, and note the choice in the constant's comment.
- **Risk (parity drift):** if `PlayScene` and `GymFormationScene` each passed a
  colour literal they could diverge. Mitigation: one shared helper + the
  defined-once equivalence guard.
- **Risk (RNG determinism):** touching the scatter helper could reorder draws.
  Mitigation: additive/optional parameter only; existing draw-order tests must
  stay green.
- **Scope-creep risk:** "while I am here" ideas (new mineral tiers, value
  changes, HUD redesign) are recorded above as out of scope, not folded in.

## Appendix: clarifying questions and answers

- **No clarifying questions were needed.** The seed context ("make the extra
  items dropped a different colour, perhaps orange") already fixes the desired
  outcome. Research resolved the remaining unknowns from the repo:
  - Salvage applies to destroyed **ships only**, not asteroids — the kill seams
    exclude non-blocking hazards (`PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene`).
  - The extra drops are already spawned (`AH-0MVH80ZJ7009W18Z`), so this is a
    rendering-only change.
  - The HUD already shows the active Salvage row, so no HUD work is required.
- **Assumptions recorded as resolved decisions:** orange = the salvage colour;
  everything else stays gold; the change is cosmetic (1 mineral per dot); the
  colour is exposed as a constant plus an optional `Mineral` config field.

# Effort and Risk Report

## Effort Estimate

- **T-shirt size:** Small
- **Three-point (PERT):** O=1.60h, M=2.60h, P=4.20h
- **Expected (E=(O+4M+P)/6):** 2.70h
- **Recommended (with overheads):** 4.50h
- **Range:** [3.40h — 6.00h]
- **Unit:** hours

### Work Breakdown Structure (WBS)

| # | Item | O (h) | M (h) | P (h) | Expected (h) |
|---|------|-------|-------|-------|-------------|
| 1 | Add MINERAL_SALVAGE_COLOR constant + optional Mineral colour | 0.40 | 0.60 | 1.00 | 0.63 |
| 2 | Shared salvage-scatter seam + PlayScene/GymFormationScene wiring + parity guard | 0.60 | 1.00 | 1.60 | 1.03 |
| 3 | Tests (Mineral + PlayScene + gym colour/parity) and docs (GDD, README) | 0.60 | 1.00 | 1.60 | 1.03 |


## Risk Assessment

- **Risk Score:** 4/25 — **Low**
- **Probability:** 2.09/5 | **Impact:** 2.09/5

## Confidence

- **Confidence:** 77%
- **Unknowns:** Exact orange hex that reads clearly against the starfield and stays distinct from enemy-bullet/pickup palettes.
- **Assumptions:** A distinct orange fill is sufficient to make the bounty legible (HUD row already exists).; An optional colour parameter keeps every existing scatterMineralDrops caller on the gold default.; RNG draw order/count in the scatter helper is unchanged.
